title: Rewriting a print-sub-plan to return
idea: return vs print: practice converting a show-only sub-plan into a compute-and-return one, then printing in the main plan.

exercises.prompt:
Start:

def area(w, h):
    print(w * h)

You now need the area to add a border later. First change?
exercises.explanation: Switch print to return so the area comes back as a value you can add to. That's the core conversion.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the converted program: area RETURNS w * h, store area(5, 2), add border 3, print the result.
exercises.explanation: Now area returns 10 into room; add 3 to get 13; print it. Converting print->return made the value reusable.
return w * h hands the area back. The main plan can then store or print it.

exercises.prompt: After converting to return, you must add a print in the MAIN plan if you still want the value shown.
exercises.explanation: Yes. return is silent, so if a human should see the value, the main plan prints the returned result.

exercises.prompt:
Predict (converted version):

def area(w, h):
    return w * h

print(area(5, 2))
exercises.explanation: area returns 10; the main plan's print shows it. Same visible result as before, but now the value is reusable.

exercises.prompt:
A classmate converts to return but forgets the main-plan print:

def area(w, h):
    return w * h

area(5, 2)

What appears on screen?
options: Nothing — the returned value isn't printed
exercises.explanation: The value 10 is handed back but nobody prints it, so the screen is blank. Add print(area(5, 2)) to show it.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: why is the returning version better here?
options: The area can be added to (border) AND printed — reusable
exercises.explanation: Returning keeps the value in play for the border math and for printing. The print-only version threw the value away.

exercises.prompt:
Convert this too:

def greet_count(n):
    print(n * 2)

You need the result to compare with 10 later. Best change?
options: Use 'return n * 2' so the result can be compared
exercises.explanation: To compare the result with 10 later, you need it as a value, so return it. Then 'if greet_count(x) > 10:' works.

exercises.prompt: Converting print to return does NOT change what the sub-plan computes — only whether the value is handed back.
exercises.explanation: Right. The math is the same; return just makes the result usable instead of only visible.

options: To make a value reusable, convert print to return — then print in the main plan if needed
exercises.explanation: Swap print for return to free the value for reuse; add a main-plan print only when a human needs to see it.
